A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gRNAde study. All 22 pages of v5 and 23 pages of v6, including equations, figures, tables, pseudocode and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial appendix reordering.

before.justification: v5 reports original gRNAde sequence-design experiments, architectural ablations and retrospective simulations of ribozyme mutant selection using published fitness data.

after.justification: v6 retains original sequence-design and ribozyme-ranking results and reports revised multi-state experiments and additional comparisons and controls.

M1.justification: The documented featurization, GVP-GNN updates, Deep Set pooling, autoregressive loss and Listing 1 are unchanged; unordered decoding was already discussed in v5. However, v6 Table 1 introduces variants labelled DSS without defining their operations. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether these represent a substantive architectural adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RNASolo collection of 4,223 sequences and 12,011 structures, the single-state and multi-state design benchmarks, and the 5TU/t1 ribozyme fitness landscapes. Additional state counts and model variants concern configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v6 adds RDesign to the 14-RNA comparison in Figure 4 and Table 2, reporting mean recovery of 0.4296; v5 compares against ViennaRNA, FARNA and Rosetta. Appendix B also newly reports a qualitative comparison with NuPack's design tool, without numerical scores. Existing external comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The stated split construction, default training budget, metrics and sampling of 16 sequences at temperature 0.1 are retained. Within this framework, v6 adds two-/four-state evaluations, random-order decoding and additional model configurations, switches the multi-state training-length ablation from one-state to three-state models, and adds an RNAFold scoring control. The all-data training/evaluation configuration is removed.

E4.justification: The ablation evidence is substantially reworked: v6 adds random-decoding-order and DS/DSS-labelled comparisons, expands multi-state non-autoregressive evaluations, and tests sensitivity to replacing EternaFold with RNAFold. It removes the solvent-accessibility analysis from v5 Figure 6 and some multi-state invariant-model ablations. The structural design case studies remain in the appendices.

E5.justification: v6 Figure 4 newly quantifies the perplexity–recovery association with Pearson correlation -0.76 and Spearman correlation -0.67. Reporting standard deviations across three consistent seeds and interquartile ranges from 10,000 random-strategy simulations is unchanged; there is no stated increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises multi-state results: the reported one-/three-/five-state autoregressive recoveries change from 0.455/0.467/0.473 to 0.481/0.531/0.510, making three states best among these configurations. Several single-state ablation values also change, RDesign and new control results are added, and all-data results are removed. The 14-RNA gRNAde recovery of 0.5682 and ribozyme-ranking results remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the cause of the broad multi-state numerical revisions.

T1.justification: The multi-graph definitions, message-passing and pooling equations, and equivariance reasoning are retained. The numerical example concerning averaging single-state predictions also remains, moving from Appendix C to Appendix F. No new theorem, proof or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The three headline contributions remain single-state design, multi-state design and zero-shot fitness ranking. v6's introduction makes the multi-state recovery claim quantitative at 5%, and its conclusion adds superiority over Rosetta in both computational and experimental performance. The latter wording is broader without a new direct experimental comparison against Rosetta.

C2.justification: v6 interprets equivariance as improving evaluation metrics, whereas v5 reported no significant differences beyond fitting the training distribution. It adds predictor-choice rationale and discussion of expensive molecular-dynamics validation, but removes the specific assay-noise caveat and the discussion of random mutagenesis as complementary local exploration. Most applicability limitations and the FAQs are retained.

D1.justification: v6 adds CPU inference timing of approximately 10 seconds and discloses over 2.8 million training nucleotides. It omits v5's explicit averaging rule for multi-state structural scores and the description of training all-data release checkpoints; this does not establish that checkpoint access was withdrawn. Core hyperparameters, pseudocode and the repository address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v6 cites Tan et al. (2023) and positions RDesign as a concurrent GNN-based inverse-folding method. The cryo-EM future-work references to Kappel et al. (2020) and Bonilla and Kieft (2022) are removed. The related-work survey otherwise remains substantively unchanged despite relocation and bibliography restyling.

P1.justification: The appendix organization is comprehensively reordered, with related work and ablations brought forward, FAQs moved to the end, and a contents list added. The inverse-folding problem subsection is merged into the opening of Section 2, and the ablation narrative is reorganized and expanded. Most main-text prose remains recognizable, but the document structure changes substantially.

P2.justification: v6 adopts different title, heading and page styling and extensively relocates displays. Figure 4 gains an RDesign bar, the multi-state figure changes from three to five state-count groups and loses its solvent-accessibility panel, and both tables are restructured. The duplicated main-text riboswitch visualization is removed while its appendix counterpart is retained.

improvement.justification: Adding a concurrent neural comparator and checks of decoding order and structure-predictor dependence modestly strengthens the empirical argument beyond v5. The benefit is limited by insufficient documentation of DSS variants, RDesign settings and the revised multi-state results. Removing the assay-noise caveat and broadening the conclusion also reduce caution, so the revision does not establish a substantial overall improvement.
